answer: Call it a rising registration ridge: each new identity must post a deposit priced from current network size, so the marginal cost climbs steeply as an attacker adds accounts; legitimate single users clear it cheaply while farms hit an accelerating bill. A light lantern check then samples each identity's linked activity to catch clusters, forfeiting deposits for the whole group once overlap appears. The reef is the resulting sunk cost, a wall of unrecoverable capital the attacker must fund before any account can act.
